requirement:
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
rationale:
The tests cover every obligation of `requirements.authoring.structural_inputs` except one: the mixed impl+test case. That gap is acknowledged by an open `{fixme}` on `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare_with_context]`, naming nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#51. I did not read the implementation source.

**Obligations mapped to tests**

Both tests are in `src/authoring/mod.rs` and carry `{test}` references to the subject.

- **Anchor and in-source `{impl}` reference both contribute, with deduplication.**
  - `structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest` declares `:impl: src/lib.rs#fn[api]` and also marks `api` with an `{impl}` comment.
  - It asserts that exactly one input has file `src/lib.rs`, with item `fn[api]`.
  - It also asserts `sources.structural`.
- **An in-source reference selects its enclosing node without an anchor.**
  - The same test removes the anchor.
  - It asserts that the unanchored mandatory inputs equal the anchored ones.
- **Whole file when there is no language outline.** The test adds `src/details.txt` with an `{impl}` reference. It asserts an input with item `""` and the full file text.
- **Refining declarations contribute complete text.** The test asserts that the `requirements.refined` input contains both paragraphs, "Complete refinement." and "Second paragraph.".
- **Helpers are not supplied recursively.** The root text contains `helper();`, and the test asserts it does not contain `fn helper`.
- **Source access, exclusions and errors follow the mandatory-input rules.** `structural_roots_obey_mandatory_access_and_resolution_rules` covers these cases:
  - An explicit disallow aborts with a "disallowed" error.
  - A missing node `fn[missing]` produces an error.
  - A generated `evidence/` anchor is omitted by default, so the review is not structural.
  - An explicit allow includes the `evidence/generated.rs` input.
  - An omitted generated `:test:` edge does not override a real implementation. With the allow, the test edge counts and the review is not structural.
- **Non-distributed only, and non-requirement subjects excluded.** The first test checks that an example subject and a requirement with `sites` are not structural.
- **A refining declaration's `{impl}` does not make its parent structural.** A requirement with only a refining declaration's reference is not structural.
- **Input staleness.** Changing the implementation root's text invalidates the recorded evidence, so the roots are real dependencies.

**Acknowledged gap**

The subject says implementation roots MUST contribute "including when the requirement also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors". The first test instead asserts the compromise behavior. With a test added, `tested.structural` is false and no `fn[api]` input is present. The same holds with a `:test:` anchor.

The `{fixme}` body says that mixed requirements omit implementation roots from the initial bundle and that the input tests assert this compromise. It also says they do not yet verify the full mixed-input contract. That is this gap, and issue #51 is open. The assertions that contradict the requirement text are therefore acknowledged, not unacknowledged.

I found no other unacknowledged gaps.

text: :::{req} structural_inputs
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
:::{req} structural_review
For every non-distributed requirement, the assessment MUST identify its stated
structural properties, including signatures, type and field relationships,
ownership, and required delegation through interfaces. With incoming `{impl}`
references or `:impl:` anchors, it MUST check that the supplied implementation
roots support every such property under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_prompt`. Without those edges, it MUST
establish that the requirement has no structural properties needing
implementation evidence; an unmet structural obligation MUST be a gap.
Incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors MUST NOT skip this check.
References and anchors are those considered under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` and the existing source-access
policy; omitted generated evidence MUST NOT count as an edge. Obligations
delegated to refining declarations follow
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`. Examples, distributed requirements,
citation reviews, and site reviews retain their own assessment tasks.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
